applies_why: The judge text adjudicates the D3 vs C6 collision, in which the witnesses pressed against the defender's Isaiah 7:14 link -- the sign's own bounds out of the challenger's Link 6 footing -- are the pressing side's own chain read together, the very situation the rule governs.
quote: the sign itself does not state the mechanism
rule_words: the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side
room: The phrase 'that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, for either side': read one way, any decision-ground of the form 'this verse does not state it in its own words' is the retired test, so the judge's 'the sign itself does not state the mechanism' as the stated reason for UNDERDETERMINED breaches; read the other way, the rule retires only weighing the pressed witnesses' silence one by one, and the judge's clause merely reports common ground while the verdict truly rests on the acknowledged chain answers (8:8 and 9:6-7 versus the sign's bounds). I adopted the first reading because the clause follows the semicolon as the judge's stated ground and the text nowhere weighs the two chains' footing.
why: The judge decided a chain-against-chain collision by one verse's silence, grounding UNDERDETERMINED on the sign's own failure to state the mechanism, which is verse-by-verse weighing with the retired stating-verse test instead of the footing comparison the rule requires.
